ForestFireR: Spatial and Mean-Field Forest-Fire Invasion Model

Source: R/ForestFireR.R
ForestFireR-package.Rd

Simulation of a two-species vegetation system in which fire mediates the competition between a native species and an invader, on an explicit lattice or in its well-mixed limit. The engine is written in C++ and exposed to R through Rcpp.

Details

See ForestFireR-model for the definition of the model: states, transitions, parameters and the mean-field equations.

To run it: generate_landscape() builds an initial spatial configuration, simulate_spatial() runs the lattice Gillespie simulation, simulate_mean_field() integrates the deterministic well-mixed limit and simulate_mean_field_stochastic() simulates the well-mixed stochastic process at a finite population size. default_rates() gives the baseline parameter set and xi2lambda() converts the dimensionless spread/regrowth probabilities into rate constants. generate_landscape_layers() and simulate_spatial_from_grid() cover initial conditions that generate_landscape() cannot express, and simulate_spatial_movie() renders a run as a video.

Worked scripts (an invasion trajectory, a landscape-clustering comparison, a fire-spread/regrowth phase diagram) are installed with the package:

list.files(system.file("examples", package = "ForestFireR"))
